concepts.title: From Kingdom to Empire
concepts.definition: An empire joins many kingdoms and peoples under one ruler; the Mauryan empire, built from Magadha, was the first to stitch most of the subcontinent into one political fabric.
concepts.key_idea: An empire is scale: what a king does for one land, an emperor must do for many lands at once.

concepts.title: Chandragupta Maurya and Kautilya
concepts.definition: Chandragupta Maurya, guided by the minister Kautilya, overthrew the Nandas and built the Mauryan empire; the Arthashastra, attributed to Kautilya, remains a manual of statecraft from that age.
concepts.key_idea: A ruler and a strategist together: the throne of Magadha plus the science of governance made an empire.

concepts.title: Ashoka and the Kalinga War
concepts.definition: Ashoka's victorious Kalinga war filled him with remorse at the suffering of war; he turned to dhamma, righteous conduct, and spread his message through edicts carved on rocks and pillars across the empire.
concepts.key_idea: The mightiest conqueror became the preacher of peace: Ashoka measured greatness in welfare, not in victories.

concepts.title: Running an Empire: Administration
concepts.definition: The empire ran through provinces and districts, graded officials, spies and a standing army, taxes on land and trade, and roads and rest houses that bound distant parts to the capital at Pataliputra.
concepts.key_idea: Administration is the empire's skeleton: officials, taxes and roads carried the ruler's word to the villages.
